Priya to produce architecture diagram for EU-only region pinning and BYOK flow (by 2026-07-02)
Customer to confirm list of required sub-processors and data categories (by 2026-06-30)
Schedule technical pilot with EU-pinned instance and sample workload (week of 2026-07-06)

header:
Date: 2026-06-25 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Sam Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (CTO - EuroPay), Marta Ruiz (Head InfoSec), Evan Chen (Legal Ops), Sofia Petrov (Infra)
summary: High-level security review focused on data residency / region pinning for EU-only processing. Customer requires EU-only data at rest and in transit for specific PII and payment metadata, wants BYOK/KMS controls, audit log retention, and a clear sub-processor list. Redwood AE/SE explained hosted vs dedicated vs private, EU-only pinned routing, options for KMS (BYOK vs Redwood-managed KMS), and proposed pilot to validate latency and cross-border risk. Agreed next steps: share SOC2/ISO docs, architecture diagram for EU-pin, list of sub-processors, and schedule pilot.
transcript: [00:00] Sam Carter: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Sam from Redwood. Did I get the time right for Lisbon? cool. We'll keep this to 45-ish minutes, mainly around data residency and region pinning requirements.

[00:18] Liam O'Connor: Yep, thanks Sam. I'm Liam, CTO at EuroPay. Marta and Evan are here from security and legal. Sofia is infra. We have fairly strict EU-only rules for payment metadata and customer PII.

[00:35] Marta Ruiz: Hi. Quick context: we're evaluating Redwood for chat summarization and embeddings but all tokens and derived vectors for EU customers must stay within EU boundaries — no cross-border copies for model training or logs. We also need KMS controls and an auditable sub-processor list.
[00:52] Priya Nair: Thanks for that. To confirm, do you need EU-only for storage at rest, processing (inference), or both? That changes options — hosted with region pinning vs Dedicated/Private.

[01:05] Marta Ruiz: Both. Processing and storage. We cannot have token-level telemetry leave the EU. Also retention policy: audit logs for 12 months, and access via SSO with RBAC. SOC 2 evidence expected.

[01:30] Sam Carter: Understood. Redwood supports region pinning — you can route all requests for a tenant to eu-west-1 only. We have dedicated capacity if you need isolated GPUs, or our hosted EU-only tenancy with pinned routing. There's nuance around backups and ephemeral caches — we'll map that out.
[01:52] Evan Chen: When you say pinned routing, is that a hard guarantee? Any chance of failover going to us-east if eu is unhealthy? We need contractual assurances about cross-border fallback.

[02:08] Priya Nair: Good question. We offer policy-based routing: by default we can set strict region-only policy — no auto-fallback to non-EU regions. For DR we can configure multi-region but only with your explicit waiver. For the pilot we can keep strict EU-only and disable cross-border fallbacks.
[02:35] Sofia Petrov: Ok, technical detail: do you spin up infra in customer VPC or is this on Redwood-managed VPC? We need to know where KMS keys live and who has access to S3 buckets etc.

[02:50] Sam Carter: Two main models — Redwood Private where you run control plane / or an on-prem package, and Dedicated where we provision a customer-dedicated cluster in our cloud account with isolation. For Dedicated we offer customer-managed VPC integration and BYOK via customer KMS, or Redwood-managed KMS if you prefer. Priya, you wanna add?

[03:08] Priya Nair: Yeah. For EU-only hosted we typically run in our eu accounts but can enable customer VPC peering for network isolation. For encryption: BYOK -> customer KMS, keys never leave KMS and we integrate via CMEK APIs. We also support HSM integrations for Private if required.

[03:30] Marta Ruiz: Sounds promising. We need to confirm whether any metadata, like request IDs or diagnostics, are sampled and sent to external telemetry that might cross border. Also how audit logs are stored and who can access them.

[03:50] Priya Nair: Default telemetry is minimal. We can disable sampling for your tenant. Audit logs are stored in the EU region, retention policy configurable — we support exports to your S3 in EU or we can provide a secure download. Access controlled via RBAC and SSO (SAML), with admin roles that you define.
[04:10] Liam O'Connor: On RBAC/SSO, can we map SCIM groups from our IdP and have just-in-time provisioning? We want least privilege for engineers vs ops vs legal.

[04:25] Sam Carter: Yes, SAML SSO + SCIM is supported, you can sync groups and assign roles. We also have audit logs for admin actions and token usage per user. There's an admin audit trail for configuration changes.

[04:40] Evan Chen: Regarding sub-processors, will you provide a current list? We need to run them through our vendor security questionnaire; any cloud infra vendors used in EU must have EU data centers only.

[04:55] Priya Nair: We'll share our sub-processor list; note that for Dedicated we minimize third-party processing — mostly cloud provider in-region and a monitoring supplier. We also have contractual addendum for data residency and sub-processor commitments.
[05:10] Marta Ruiz: About KMS: if we do BYOK, who can rotate keys? And can Redwood perform operations like re-encrypt for upgrades without keys leaving our control?

[05:25] Priya Nair: With BYOK, you control key lifecycle in your KMS. Redwood requests decrypt/encrypt operations via API calls — keys never leave your KMS. For provider upgrades we don't extract plaintext; we rewrap tokens using KMS APIs. We can provide an architecture doc for the crypto flow.

[05:50] Sam Carter: Also, for compliance evidence: SOC 2 Type II report covers our controls. We'll provide the report and an ISO 27001 summary. Note some redactions may apply for third-party info but the main controls will be in the package.
[06:05] Liam O'Connor: Do you have a data processing addendum (DPA) that covers GDPR and explicit EU data residency clauses?
[06:15] Sam Carter: Yes, standard DPA with GDPR clauses and we can add a residency appendix specifying EU-only processing for the scope of the contract.

[06:30] Sofia Petrov: A couple of gotchas: model caching and KV cache — is it stored in ephemeral memory on the GPU host or persisted to disk in EU region? Because some of our workflows cause KV to be spilled to disk.

[06:48] Priya Nair: Good point. By default KV cache is in-memory; for large contexts we may spill to local disk. For EU-only requirement we ensure any spill is to disks provisioned in EU and we can mount disks in customer VPC or encrypted volumes managed by your KMS.
[07:05] Marta Ruiz: What about backups or snapshots that Redwood takes for maintenance? Are those replicated outside EU by default?

[07:18] Sam Carter: Snapshots and backups for EU-pinned tenants are configured to remain in EU by default. If you opt into cross-region DR we would need explicit consent. We'll provide the snapshot policy in the architecture doc.
[07:36] Evan Chen: On audit logs: we need immutable retention for 12 months and the ability to export to our SIEM. Can logs be shipped to customer S3 in eu-west-1 and to our Splunk instance?
[07:50] Priya Nair: Yes, we can push logs to customer-owned S3 in eu-west-1, and we have connectors to common SIEMs. Exports happen over TLS and the data stays in-region.
[08:06] Liam O'Connor: Are there any sub-processors outside EU involved in model inference? For example, model providers or telemetry vendors based in US?

[08:20] Priya Nair: Our curated model catalog includes open models and self-hosted variants; inference for EU-pinned tenant runs in EU compute. We don't call external inference APIs for content processing. Telemetry vendors are optional and can be disabled; default telemetry is retained in-region.
[08:40] Marta Ruiz: We also need to know about legal process — subpoenas or government access. If data is stored in EU, what's Redwood's stance if a US-based legal request arrives?

[08:55] Sam Carter: If data is stored in EU and not replicated outside, requests outside EU would not grant Redwood access to EU data. We follow legal process and inform customers; specifics covered in DPA and law enforcement guidelines.
[09:12] Evan Chen: Can you confirm if any developer logs or crash dumps ever include customer payloads? We want PII redaction by default.
[09:27] Priya Nair: Crash dumps are scrubbed of payloads by default; we can apply stricter PII redaction for your tenant. We'll document scrub rules in the security package.

[09:45] Sam Carter: Quick note on performance: dedicated EU clusters will give you lowest latency; Hosted EU-pinned is still fine but shared tenancy might have slightly higher p99s. We'll include benchmark numbers.
[10:05] Liam O'Connor: What's the expected impact on tokens cost and latency if we enable strict EU-only and BYOK? Any significant premiums?

[10:18] Priya Nair: Minimal for region pinning. BYOK doesn't change token costs; Dedicated compute may be pricier but predictable. The bigger cost is Dedicated reserved capacity vs hosted shared. We'll run cost projections in the proposal.
[10:36] Marta Ruiz: About sub-processors again — can we get a monthly updated list and notification of changes? We need time to review before they go into scope.
[10:48] Sam Carter: We provide a sub-processor notification process; changes trigger a notification email and a 30-day review window for contract customers. We'll include that clause in the DPA.

[11:05] Sofia Petrov: For the pilot, we'll want a small test dataset from EU customers and measure latency and any cross-border flags. Is there a safe way to run that without sharing production PII? We'll use synthetic but realistic samples.
[11:22] Priya Nair: Synthetic data is perfect; we'll provide test harness and small client to route to EU-pinned endpoint. Priya will run a throughput test and give p50/p95/p99 numbers.

[11:38] Liam O'Connor: On the legal side, if we sign a contract with EU residency appendix, do you accept that as contractual guarantee that no data will exit EU for that tenant? We need explicit language.

[11:52] Sam Carter: Yes, we can add an EU residency appendix that restricts processing and storage to EU regions only and disallows cross-border replication without written consent. We'll have legal draft it after this call.
[12:08] Evan Chen: For the SOC 2 report, will you share a sealed copy or is it downloadable? We usually require the Type II with the period covered noted.
[12:18] Sam Carter: We'll share the Type II report with standard NDAs/redactions as needed. I'll drop the secure link in the CRM and share with your legal ops.

[12:35] Marta Ruiz: One more technical: how do you handle model updates that may change behavior of cached embeddings — do you keep older model artifacts or might that cause data to be reprocessed outside EU during onboarding?

[12:50] Priya Nair: Model rollouts are throttled; for EU tenants we pin model versions and rollouts are controlled. We won't migrate data cross-border. If you want automatic upgrades we can do them in-region under strict change control.
[13:08] Sam Carter: We're coming up on 35 minutes — is there anything else?
[13:12] Marta Ruiz: I want to confirm the audit trail for admin changes — can we get an S3 export nightly?
[13:20] Priya Nair: Yes, nightly exports to your EU S3 are supported; we can provide format and schema. We'll also surface admin changes in the console with timestamps and user IDs.
[13:36] Evan Chen: Please include the legal contact for Redwood for DPA discussions so we can loop them in.
[13:44] Sam Carter: Will do. I'll include our legal contact in the follow-up email along with the security pack.
[13:55] Liam O'Connor: Any risks we might have overlooked regarding sub-processors at the OS level? For instance, if monitoring agent is US-based but collects only EU logs, still an issue?

[14:10] Priya Nair: That's why we minimize third parties; monitoring can be set to in-region endpoints; if a vendor is US-based but hosts EU endpoints it's acceptable with contractual guarantees. We'll mark any such vendors in the sub-processor list.

[14:30] Marta Ruiz: Good. For the pilot, our success criteria: data never leaves EU, BYOK works end-to-end, audit logs exported to our S3, and latency within 20% of baseline. If that passes we proceed to contract.
[14:50] Sam Carter: Sounds reasonable. We'll aim for that. Any objections to scheduling the pilot week of July 6th?
[15:00] Liam O'Connor: July 6th works for us, pending internal sign-off. Evan will confirm legal availability.
[15:10] Evan Chen: I'll check and loop back by Tuesday.

[15:20] Sam Carter: Great — recap: Sam sends SOC2+ISO and legal contact, Priya publishes EU-arch doc and runs test, customer returns sub-processor list and data categories. We'll put all items in CRM and follow up with calendar invite for pilot. Anything else?
[15:36] Marta Ruiz: No, that's it from security. Thank you.
[15:40] Liam O'Connor: Thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.
[15:44] Sam Carter: Thanks all, talk soon — bye.
[47:30] <call ended>
